cards.def: The government must show the law serves a compelling interest and is narrowly tailored to achieve it by the least restrictive means. Applied to content-based speech restrictions.
A law that regulates speech because of the subject matter or viewpoint expressed. Presumptively unconstitutional and reviewed under strict scrutiny.
A content-neutral rule on when, where, or how speech happens. Valid if narrowly tailored to a significant government interest and leaving open ample alternative channels.
Advocacy of illegal action is protected unless it is directed to inciting imminent lawless action and is likely to produce it.
Government action barring speech before it occurs. Carries a heavy presumption against constitutional validity.
Government property historically open to expressive activity, such as streets and parks. Content-based restrictions there face strict scrutiny.
A law is facially invalid if it prohibits a substantial amount of protected speech relative to its legitimate sweep, even as applied to this speaker's unprotected conduct.
Public schools may restrict student speech only when it would materially and substantially disrupt schoolwork or discipline, or invade the rights of others.
